purpose: Evaluate the minimal typed replay IR v5 pyenv semantic normalization on the four audited Round2 EnvSolve v0 trajectories that triggered the rule, without new model calls or source-run mutation.
claim_scope: Development-informed mechanism qualification only; this experiment is not confirmatory and does not estimate held-out generalization.

source.selection_rule: Include every Round2 envsolve_v0 record with valid harness audit, passing v0 completion boundary, unsafe_or_unreplayable_action outcome, and exact pyenv init rejection. Exclude repository-integrity failures.

precommitted_expectations.redistillation: Exactly two of four trajectories should become fully replayable under the single v5 rule; the other two should remain fail-closed due to independently unsupported actions.
precommitted_expectations.official_outcome: Report official outcomes for every trajectory that reaches evaluation. No minimum pass count is precommitted because v5 repairs representation rather than environment solving.
precommitted_expectations.interpretation: An official pass would show that v4 hid a valid solved environment. An official failure would localize a remaining replay or verifier-equivalence gap. Neither outcome is held-out evidence for the future EnvSolve algorithm.

validity_requirements: All source case identities, trajectory hashes, source audits, repository integrity records, and passing v0 completion boundaries match the frozen source artifacts
No model or provider request occurs
Typed replay IR v5 and harness v3 hashes match before execution
All four source trajectories are attempted exactly once without overwrite
No replay grammar, integrity policy, evaluator, or case-specific rule changes during the batch
stop_rule: Collect all four first attempts, audit them, and publish both successful and rejected redistillations before any further mechanism change.
